solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Combative sport in a ring enthralling one child

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a kid is a child
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A boxing match where a fighter's youngster is spellbound by what happens in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art, a form of self-defence combat practised as a sport.

clue.text: What provides illumination correctly around walls of cell

indicators.note: the word for correctly goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: aright means correctly, rightly

indicators.note: the walls of a cell are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Asks what lights a prison cell properly, round its walls.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp gives intense light from an electric arc, used in film studios and searchlights.

clue.text: The most important person appears in shocking pink

indicators.note: the answer appears inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A VIP shows up dressed in a loud, shocking pink outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the central figure on whom everything depends, the boss.

clue.text: Cruel old character upset Biblical town to the north

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: a card is an eccentric character

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: Nain is the Galilean town where Jesus raised a widow's son

explanation.surface: An old villain causes trouble in a town mentioned in the Bible, up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OCARD into DRACO; 'to the north' turns NAIN into NIAN. Draco was the Athenian lawgiver whose harsh code gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian laws are excessively harsh, so the adjective is a synonym for cruel or severe.

clue.text: Party leader and upper-class member of cabinet likely to benefit from Eton, say?

definitions.text: likely to benefit from Eton, say?

parts.note: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party when this was set
U is the label for upper-class usage
Vince Cable sat in the coalition cabinet as Business Secretary

explanation.surface: Political figures of 2011, with a dig at the Old Etonians running the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is England's best-known private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educable is capable of being taught, so would profit from schooling such as Eton provides.

clue.text: Record how old we are — that's intended, we hear, to create gloom

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
our age is how old we are

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are taken as spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Someone noting their age, which they intend to be depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Discouragement is a loss of confidence or hope, a downcast state close to gloom.

clue.text: Youngster with oomph? 25 many years ago!

parts.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
it is sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A lively youngster exclaims about some distant past.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is MEASURE: the definition says a measure used long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The cubit was an ancient length unit, roughly forearm length, used in Biblical times.

clue.text: Sort of music slowing down on piano — dance around

indicators.note: the dance goes around the other two pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to bop is to dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction for slowing down
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A musician slowing down at the piano while people dance round.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was a 1990s British guitar-pop genre of bands like Oasis and Blur.

clue.text: Revelation of former model

parts.note: ex means former
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A former model tells all in a tabloid revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposé is a report that reveals something scandalous, a public disclosure.

clue.text: Feature of theatre is terrible muncher, so I carp

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatregoer complains about the dreadful snack-muncher in the next seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The proscenium arch frames the stage opening in a traditional theatre, separating stage from audience.

clue.text: Birmingham arena about to get one lot of stars and another

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the arena's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham
another lot of stars: Taurus, the Bull constellation

explanation.surface: A Birmingham venue is about to welcome one group of pop stars and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurus is a southern constellation, a group of stars pictured as a centaur.

clue.text: A particular colonel that may be used in advertising

definitions.meaning: Colonel ..., David Low's cartoon of a pompous reactionary officer

definitions.text: that may be used in advertising
definitions.meaning: an airship, tethered or flying, carrying slogans

explanation.surface: A colonel who might appear in an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Blimp gave his name to reactionary types; a blimp is also a non-rigid airship carrying ads.

clue.text: Wicked trouble-maker is hanging round prestigious academic institution

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous troublemaker

indicators.note: the word is hangs round the institution, enclosing it

parts.note: OU is short for Oxford University

explanation.surface: A troublemaker loitering around a top university.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, hence sinful or wicked.

clue.text: Firm turned round by leading American who has great influence?

indicators.note: turned round means the short word for a firm is reversed

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
top means leading, first
US means American

explanation.surface: A company taken over by a powerful American tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an octopus is an organisation whose tentacles reach everywhere, wielding wide influence.

clue.text: In the capital a leader wants hearts first and foremost

indicators.note: says the hearts piece comes at the very front

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts
No. 1, written NO and I, is the leader, as at the top of the charts

explanation.surface: A card player in a capital city wants to lead hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam.

clue.text: Evidence of sorrow? Time to get out liquid medication

indicators.note: the time letter is made to get out of the longer word, leaving it

parts.note: teardrops show someone is sad

explanation.surface: Someone's tears suggest it is time to fetch a soothing medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear drops are a liquid medicine dripped into the ear.

clue.text: Clothe the old woman, character creating fuss

parts.note: to rig out is to clothe
the old woman is slang for mother, ma
a role is a character in a play

explanation.surface: Dressing up an old woman as a stage character, a palaver.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, tedious, complicated procedure, a lot of fuss.

clue.text: Magnificent organ (though with one note missing) sufficed

indicators.note: missing says the note is lost from the organ's name

parts.note: the spleen is an organ of the body
E is one of the musical notes
did means sufficed, as in 'that did'

explanation.surface: An organ played with one note dead still did the job splendidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid is a synonym of magnificent: impressive, grand, brilliant.

clue.text: Parts to bring for labelling with specific identity

indicators.note: parts means splits apart the word bring so something can go between

parts.note: taken as written
to here works as and, as in adding one thing to another

explanation.surface: Instructions on which components to bring for marking items with identity labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun meaning components, but it is a verb: it splits the next word open. 'To' stands for 'and' as in 'add this to that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Branding is marking a product with a distinctive name or logo that identifies it.

clue.text: Big bird embraces bloke — start of exciting novel?

indicators.note: the bird embraces the bloke, holding him inside

parts.note: the roc is a huge mythical bird
a man is a bloke

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A giant bird clutching a man: the opening of an adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a kind of novel, a story of love or adventure; the question mark signals an example.

clue.text: Stir created by special outfit

definitions.meaning: to stir is to rise from bed in the morning
a costume or rig worn for an occasion

explanation.surface: A fuss caused by a remarkable costume.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up is to stir from sleep; a getup is an elaborate or unusual outfit.

clue.text: Ex-PM making honest money from what's reported

indicators.note: what's reported means the words are taken as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: true means honest and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A former prime minister earning a clean living, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Trudeau was Prime Minister of Canada, so in 2011 a former premier.

clue.text: Private hospital or home swamped by endless sound

indicators.note: swamped by means the home word is engulfed inside the other
endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a click is a short sharp sound
in means at home

explanation.surface: A private hospital, or perhaps a house drowned in noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical establishment, often a private hospital or specialist centre.

clue.text: Religion to make an impact on society in the end

parts.note: to lam is to strike hard, hit

indicators.note: society goes in the word for end, inside it

parts.note: an aim is an end, an objective

explanation.surface: A faith whose purpose is ultimately to make its mark on society.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamaism is an older name for Tibetan Buddhism, led by lamas.

clue.text: At university this idle? Erupt!

parts.note: UP means at university; the answer read as two words says UP goes ..., which makes the clue's last word

explanation.surface: A student told to stop lazing about and burst into action.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: putting UP (at university) in ERT gives ERUPT, the clue's final word.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless, inactive, sluggish: a close synonym of idle.

clue.text: A word of significance to the egotist to a certain extent

parts.words: A word of significance to the egotist
parts.note: an egotist's favourite word is me
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An egotist's favourite word matters to a certain degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Measure means size or extent, as in 'beyond measure'.

clue.text: Like a coined word to denote 'Christian but not Anglican'?

parts.note: non means not
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: Suggests a coinage meaning a Christian outside the Church of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NON-CE it would describe a Christian not of the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonce word is coined for one occasion, so nonce describes such a coinage.

clue.text: Small animal — does 'e sadly fail to grow properly?

parts.note: a runt is the smallest animal of a litter

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks whether the weakling of the litter will fail to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To run to seed is to go into decline, as a plant that bolts stops growing usefully.

clue.text: Wild beasts running in the chase

indicators.note: running suggests letters set loose and moving, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild animals racing along in pursuit of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheetahs are big wild cats, the fastest land animals.

clue.text: Return looking embarrassed, merriment stifled

indicators.note: stifled means the merriment is smothered inside the other word

parts.note: red-faced, so red
fun is merriment

explanation.surface: A blushing customer, no longer amused, asks for their money back.
explanation.definitionFit: A refund is a return of money paid.
